newsitem.title: USA: Cisco, Alcatel in Internet voice, data pact.
newsitem.headline: Cisco, Alcatel in Internet voice, data pact.

text.p: Alcatel Telecom and Cisco Systems Inc. said Monday they agreed to form a strategic partnership to develop equipment using current and new technologies to integrate the Internet with phone networks.

The pact, which builds on the companies' existing sales partnership, marks an unprecedented level of cooperation between a major telephone equipment supplier and the top supplier of Internet transmission equipment, analysts said.

While Cisco has links with various telecom equipment makers, the latest partnership covers not just a single product or technology but a full range of voice and data systems in use or under consideration by phone carriers.
At a news conference in New York, Cisco President John Chambers said he expected the partnership to result in more than $500 million in additional revenues for Cisco within three years.

"By the year 2000 it ought to result in $500 million plus of incremental revenue that would not have come to us otherwise," Chambers said, adding that Cisco only forms such high-level partnerships when it can expect such returns.
Cisco posted revenues of more than $6 billion in 1996.

But analysts cautioned the move could make for frostier ties with Lucent Technologies Inc. and Northern Telecom Ltd., two traditional phone network suppliers that have begun targeting Cisco's data networking stronghold.

"It helps Cisco move further into the carrier network business, but it raises questions about what happens to Cisco relationships with Alcatel's rivals," Prudential analyst Luke Szymczak said. "Still this is significant news for Cisco."
Cisco rose about 44 cents to $69.81 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue with 11.5 million shares traded.

Alcatel Telecom is owned by Alcatel Alsthom, the French engineering conglomerate. Cisco dominates the market for data networking equipment in large corporations and its products are gaining ground among telephone carriers. Cisco boasts that 80 percent of all Internet traffic runs over its equipment.
The non-exclusive partnership would result in 10 to 12 products over the next two years covering a range of communications technologies offered by the companies.

Significantly, Alcatel said it would integrate Cisco's basic operating system software into key products used by telecom service providers, making Cisco's Internet routing technology an essential part of Alcatel phone networks.
In return, Cisco plans to integrate Alcatel's technology for transfering phone calls in offices into combined voice and data networks that Cisco offers to businesses.
Cisco will also use high-speed data technology Alcatel is developing for four U.S. regional Bell phone companies.

Chambers said Alcatel is one of nine to 10 major strategic partners that Cisco plans to work with in coming years as part of a broad strategy to form partnerships with only a select number of technology suppliers and service providers.
Cisco has set up major partnerships with technology providers Intel Corp. in semiconductors, Microsoft Corp. in software, Hewlett-Packard Co. for computer systems and now Alcatel for phone networks.
Last month, Cisco announced a pact with phone service provider GTE Corp. to create integrated voice and data network systems valued at more than $1 billion.
Chambers said he expects to announce several additional strategic partnerships in the next 12 to 18 months.
